Finite difference

 Home Mathematics Area of mathematics Analysis Numerical analysis
OurBigBook.com Words: 5k Articles: 103
A finite difference compares the values of a function at finitely separated arguments. For example, the forward finite difference with step h is
Δh​f(x)=f(x+h)−f(x).
(1)
It is the discrete analogue of a derivative and lowers the degree of a nonconstant polynomial by one.

Finite difference coefficient

Words: 34
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
Finite difference coefficients are the weights in a linear combination of sampled function values approximating a derivative. Matching polynomial moments determines the weights and approximation order. Forward, backward and centered stencils have different coefficients.

Mehrstellen method (D9​U=(I+12h2​D5​)f)

Words: 129 Articles: 1
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
A Mehrstellen method increases the accuracy of a compact finite difference method discretization by using the differential equation to express its leading truncation terms in terms of the prescribed source. For Δu=f, the square-grid nine-point finite-difference stencil for the Laplacian satisfies D9​u=Δu+h2Δ2u/12+O(h4). Replacing Δ2u by Δf and approximating this source derivative gives D9​U=(I+h2D5​/12)f, with fourth-order normalized consistency of a numerical method while retaining a compact nine-point matrix. The uncorrected nine-point finite-difference stencil operator is only second-order accurate on general functions.

Compact semidiscrete nine-point diffusion (Mh​U˙=Lh​U)

Words: 63
Mehrstellen method OurBigBook.com
On a square grid, let Ch​ sum the four axial neighbors and Kh​ the four diagonal neighbors. With Mh​=2I/3+Ch​/12 and Lh​=(−10I/3+2Ch​/3+Kh​/6)/h2, the method of lines has fourth-order normalized spatial numerical consistency. Its mass symbol is (4+cosξ+cosη)/6≥1/3, and its diffusion symbol is [−10+4(cosξ+cosη)+2cosξcosη]/(3h2)≤0. Every continuous-time mode therefore contracts, and Parseval identity gives mesh-independent discrete L2 stability. No time-step restriction is involved until a time integrator is selected.

Rational implicit advection stencil with exact shift exceptions (μ=Δt/Δx)

Words: 79
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
Consider a one-step stencil with new-level coefficients a=μ(1+μ)/2, b=(1+μ)(2−μ) and c=(1−μ)(2−μ)/2 at offsets −1,0,1, and old-level coefficients d=2−μ, e=1+μ at offsets 0,1. For ut​=ux​, its exact-solution residual starts at fourth degree with coefficient μ(μ−2)(μ−1)(μ+1)/24. Thus its normalized local truncation error is third order at fixed nonzero Courant number, except at the exact-shift values −1,1,2; zero gives the zero-step identity. For its Fourier symbol, ∣D∣2−∣N∣2=μ(μ−2)(μ−1)(μ+1)(1−cosθ)2. Uniformly invertible stable steps occur for μ≤−1, 0≤μ≤1 or μ≥2.

Centered discrete advection is skew-adjoint (Re⟨u,D0​u⟩h​=0)

Words: 59
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
With zero endpoints, the centered first-difference matrix has opposite off-diagonal entries and is a skew-adjoint operator in the mesh-weighted Euclidean inner product. Adding a real multiple of it to the negative symmetric second-difference matrix does not change the real energy form. The semidiscrete convection-diffusion solution therefore obeys a mesh-independent energy estimate, even when its drift is large compared with its diffusion coefficient.

Positive definiteness of the grounded nine-point Poisson stencil (uTAu=∑wij​(ui​−uj​)2)

Words: 106
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
On a rectangular grid with zero Dirichlet boundary conditions, the nine-point Poisson equation matrix has diagonal 10/3, axial off-diagonal entries −2/3, and diagonal-neighbor entries −1/6. Its quadratic form is the sum of squared differences over internal links, weighted by 2/3 or 1/6, plus the weighted squares of values linked to the fixed zero boundary. The connected axial grid forces a zero quadratic form to have all entries zero. This proves positive-definite matrix in every ordering. The Jacobi method converges because its nonnegative iteration matrix has row sums at most one, with a strict deficit at boundary-adjacent vertices; a hypothetical unit-modulus eigenvector would propagate its maximum modulus to such a deficit row, which is impossible.

Implicit advection scheme with exact integer shifts (μ∈(−∞,−1]∪[0,1]∪[2,∞))

Words: 91
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
A three-point implicit advection stencil can match translated data through cubic Taylor expansion while retaining a rational Fourier amplification symbol. For the coefficient family a=μ(1+μ)/6, b=(2−μ)(1+μ)/3, c=(2−μ)(1−μ)/6, d=(2−μ)/3, e=(1+μ)/3, its factor is G=(d+eeiθ)/(ae−iθ+b+ceiθ). Direct subtraction gives ∣D∣2−∣N∣2=μ(μ−2)(μ−1)(μ+1)(1−cosθ)2/9. The displayed ranges are the contraction ranges in the discrete L2 norm, with a nonvanishing denominator there. For forward time and positive speed parameter, retain the nonnegative ranges. For fixed nonzero nonexceptional Courant number, the normalized truncation error is third order; at μ=−1,0,1,2 the update is the corresponding exact grid translation.

Lax-Friedrichs method

Words: 39
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
For ut​+cux​=0 on a uniform grid, the update Umn+1​=(Um−1n​+Um+1n​)/2−ν(Um+1n​−Um−1n​)/2 has symbol cosθ−iνsinθ, where ν=cΔt/h. Its squared modulus is 1+(ν2−1)sin2θ, giving contraction exactly for ∣ν∣≤1. Stability is separate from the dissipative and dispersive approximation errors.

L2-compatible initialization of grid data

Words: 130 Articles: 1
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
An arbitrary L2 initial function has no well-defined nodal point samples. Cell averages or a bounded projection to the discrete approximation space supply grid data independently of its pointwise representative. Jensen's inequality bounds the cell-average discrete L2 norm by the continuous L2 norm. Combining consistent bounded initialization, stability, and density of smooth data can extend convergence to rough initial functions, without claiming their nonexistent classical derivatives.

Cell-average projection (Um​=h−1∫xm​−h/2xm​+h/2​u(x)dx)

Words: 69
L2-compatible initialization of grid data OurBigBook.com
The cell-average projection replaces a function by its average on each grid cell. It is independent of the representative of an L2 function, unlike point sampling. The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives h∣Um​∣2≤∫cell m​∣u∣2dx, hence h∑m​∣Um​∣2≤∥u∥L22​. Viewed as a piecewise constant function, the projection is the orthogonal projection onto the grid's piecewise constant linear subspace. Density of continuous compactly supported functions and the contraction estimate give convergence in the L2 norm as the mesh tends to zero.

Words: 122 Articles: 1
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
On a periodic uniform grid, shifting an index in the discrete inner product gives the displayed skew-adjoint identity for the centered first difference. It also gives ⟨U,Dxx​V⟩h​=−⟨D+​U,D+​V⟩h​. With finite boundaries there are additional boundary terms unless the prescribed endpoint traces eliminate them. These identities are discrete counterparts of integration by parts and prove energy estimates for finite difference methods.

Evaluating a variable diffusion coefficient at both adjacent half-grid points makes odd spatial Taylor terms cancel. The conservative spatial bracket is h2(aux​)x​+O(h4), yielding a fourth-order one-step residual when the forward time step is proportional to h2.

Monotone half-grid diffusion update (k≤h2/(2β))

Words: 81
Symmetric half-grid diffusion consistency OurBigBook.com
For 0<a(x)≤β, the explicit conservative diffusion update has weights kam−1/2​/h2, 1−k(am−1/2​+am+1/2​)/h2, and kam+1/2​/h2. Under the displayed restriction they are nonnegative and sum to one. With zero Dirichlet boundary conditions, each new value is a convex combination of old interior and boundary values, proving contraction in the discrete maximum norm. The spatial matrix is also symmetric with vTLh​v=−h−2∑am+1/2​(vm+1​−vm​)2. This puts its eigenvalues in [−4β/h2,0], so the same restriction gives L2 norm contraction. A stable recurrence need not be consistent with a different proposed differential equation.

Upwind finite difference scheme

Words: 147 Articles: 1
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
For constant-speed advection ut​+aux​=0 with a>0, the explicit upwind scheme uses Ujn+1​=(1−ν)Ujn​+νUj−1n​, ν=ak/h. For a<0 the neighbour must be on the other side. When 0≤ν≤1, the update is a convex combination and is contractive in the maximum norm on a periodic grid, or with appropriate controlled inflow data.
On a periodic grid, von Neumann stability analysis gives G=1−ν+νe−iθ and ∣G∣2=1−2ν(1−ν)(1−cosθ), proving the same exact contraction range in the discrete L2 norm. Boundary estimates are still required on a finite interval; stable scalar eigenvalues of a triangular boundary update alone need not give a mesh-uniform bound.

Five-point heat-reaction stability threshold (κ≤8h−2sin2(πh/2))

Five-point Laplacian OurBigBook.com
On a unit-square uniform mesh with h=1/(M+1) and zero Dirichlet boundary conditions, the semidiscrete five-point Laplacian has eigenvalues −4h−2[sin2(jπh/2)+sin2(kπh/2)]. Adding reaction κI gives a contractive continuous-time grid evolution exactly under the displayed threshold. The threshold is 2π2−π4h2/6+O(h4), slightly below the continuum threshold. This is an all-time non-growth criterion; finite-time mesh-uniform bounds also hold for fixed larger reaction rates.

Nine-point finite-difference stencil OurBigBook.com
For the Dirichlet discrete Laplacian on a square, let T=h−2tridiag(1,−2,1). The standard axial five-point operator is T⊗I+I⊗T, and the axial-weight 2/3, corner-weight 1/6 nine-point operator additionally contains h2T⊗T/6. Its eigenvalues are therefore strictly larger than the five-point values for the same sine modes. Both lie above the corresponding negative continuum Laplacian eigenvalues, so the five-point operator has smaller spectral error. For fixed mode numbers the leading errors are respectively π4h2(k4+l4)/12 and π4h2(k2+l2)2/12.

Compact fourth-order Helmholtz stencil (h−2Γ9​u+λMh​u=0)

Words: 82
Nine-point finite-difference stencil OurBigBook.com
Let Γ9​ have center weight −10/3, axial weights 2/3 and diagonal weights 1/6, and let Mh​ have center weight 2/3 and axial weights 1/12. Taylor expansion gives h−2Γ9​u=Δu+h2Δ2u/12+O(h4) and Mh​u=u+h2Δu/12+O(h4). On a smooth solution of the constant-coefficient Helmholtz equation, the second-order term becomes h2Δ(Δu+λu)/12=0. Thus the normalized PDE residual is fourth order, while the original unscaled stencil residual is sixth order. This local cancellation alone does not prove uniform global accuracy at or near a resonance.

Jacobi convergence for the nine-point Dirichlet stencil (ρ(I−D−1A)<1)

Words: 70
Nine-point finite-difference stencil OurBigBook.com
The Jacobi method has axial neighbour weights 1/5 and diagonal weights 1/20. Interior row sums are one, boundary-adjacent sums are smaller, and the positive-weight graph is connected. If an eigenvalue had modulus one, a maximal-modulus eigenvector component would force all its neighbours to have the same modulus. Propagation reaches a deficient row, a contradiction. This proves strict spectral-radius control even though the infinity norm of the iteration matrix can equal one.

Simultaneous row and column permutations preserve symmetry and negative definiteness.

D=(I−μAx​)−1(I+μ2Ax​Ay​)(I−μAy​)−1.
(41)
Its common-basis eigenvalues are
dpq​=(1−μλp​)(1−μλq​)1+μ2λp​λq​​.
(42)
Since λp​,λq​<0, one has 0<dpq​≤1 for every μ>0.

Seven-point Dirichlet Laplacian

Words: 45
Dirichlet discrete Laplacian OurBigBook.com
On a three-dimensional Cartesian grid, the seven-point Dirichlet Laplacian adds the six nearest-neighbour values and subtracts six times the central value. Extending a grid vector by zero on the boundary gives the discrete energy identity
vTLh​v=−∑{i,j} grid edge​(vi​−vj​)2,
(43)
so its matrix is symmetric negative definite.

Centered convection-diffusion semidiscretization

Words: 35
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
With homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, centered differences turn one-dimensional diffusion into a symmetric negative-definite matrix and constant advection into a skew-symmetric matrix. Their sum dissipates the discrete Euclidean norm, giving mesh-uniform energy stability for every fixed advection coefficient.

Discrete maximum principle

Words: 38
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
A discrete elliptic operator satisfies a discrete maximum principle when a grid function with nonnegative discrete Laplacian cannot have a positive interior maximum unless it is constant. It yields uniqueness and max-norm stability estimates for Dirichlet finite-difference problems.

Method of lines

Words: 396 Articles: 5
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
The method of lines discretizes space in a time-dependent partial differential equation while leaving time continuous, producing a finite system of ordinary differential equations.

Dissipative second-order forward advection semidiscretization (um′​=h−1(−3um​/2+2um+1​−um+2​/2))

Words: 60
Method of lines OurBigBook.com
For periodic indexing let S be the unitary forward shift. The operator is A=−3I/2+2S−S2/2. A discrete Fourier transform diagonalizes it with eigenvalue λ(θ)=−3/2+2eiθ−e2iθ/2 and real part −(1−cosθ)2. Consequently ∥etA/h∥2​≤1 for every t≥0, uniformly in the grid. Equivalently A+A∗=−21​(2I−S−S∗)2, proving decay of the discrete energy directly. The result is semidiscrete stability; a further time discretization must also have adequate absolute stability.

Energy contraction for centered drift-diffusion (dtd​∥U∥h2​=−h2​∑j​∣Uj+1​−Uj​∣2≤0)

Words: 69
Method of lines OurBigBook.com
For homogeneous Dirichlet endpoints, the centered first-difference matrix is skew-Hermitian and the centered second-difference matrix is negative definite. Thus U˙=(Dxx​−αDx​)U is contractive in the discrete L2 norm for every real α and every mesh width. The displayed identity follows by summation by parts. Nonnegative off-diagonal entries additionally require ∣α∣h≤2; that maximum-principle condition is not necessary for the L2 energy estimate. numerical consistency and Duhamel's formula then give second-order numerical convergence for smooth solutions and compatible initial approximations.

Displacement stability of a symmetric semidiscrete wave equation

Words: 190 Articles: 1
Method of lines OurBigBook.com
Let Kh​ be a symmetric nonnegative matrix and consider U′′=(αI−Kh​)U with fixed real α. In any inner product for which Kh​ is self-adjoint, diagonalization of a matrix gives
∥U(t)∥≤emax(α,0)​t(∥U(0)∥+t∥U′(0)∥).
(44)
Indeed each modal coefficient is either a cosine and sine divided by its frequency, a linear function at zero frequency, or a hyperbolic cosine and sine divided by its growth rate. The bounds ∣cos(ωt)∣≤1, ∣sin(ωt)/ω∣≤t, and sinh(βt)/β≤teβt prove the estimate. It is uniform in the spectrum of Kh​ and therefore gives finite-time displacement stability. Uniform velocity estimates need additional control of the initial spatial energy. All-time displacement bounds require a strictly positive lower bound for Kh​−αI, a different condition.
All-time boundedness of a semidiscrete reaction wave equation (α<λmin​(Kh​))
Words: 74
Displacement stability of a symmetric semidiscrete wave equation OurBigBook.com
For U′′=(αI−Kh​)U with symmetric positive definite Kh​, all-data displacement is bounded for all time on a fixed grid exactly when α<λmin​(Kh​). Diagonalization of a matrix reduces this assertion to oscillators. At equality, an initial velocity in a zero-frequency mode produces linear growth; above it a growing hyperbolic mode is available. A lower bound on λmin​(Kh​)−α uniform in the mesh gives a uniform displacement estimate. This all-time statement is stronger than displacement stability of a symmetric semidiscrete wave equation on fixed finite time intervals.

Norm conservation of a semidiscrete Schrödinger equation (iU′=HU, H=H∗ ⟹ ∥U(t)∥=∥U(0)∥)

Words: 53
Method of lines OurBigBook.com
If a spatial method of lines has a Hermitian matrix H, its generator −iH is a skew-Hermitian matrix. The matrix exponential e−itH is a unitary matrix, so it preserves the Euclidean norm and any constant-volume discrete L2 norm. Equivalently, differentiating the squared norm gives 2Re(−iU∗HU)=0. A real sampled potential preserves the Hermitian property of a symmetric discrete Laplacian. Subsequent time discretization must be assessed separately.

Lax equivalence theorem

Words: 16
Finite difference method OurBigBook.com
For a well-posed linear initial-value problem and a consistent finite-difference approximation, stability is equivalent to convergence.
